"REDACT" : raw.action; if (raw.decision !== undefined && raw.decision !== decision) { throw new Error("Inconsistent guard decision"); } if (["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action)) { const replacement = raw.safeText ?? raw.redactedText; if (typeof replacement !== "string" || !replacement.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing usable guard replacement"); } } } return response; // Preserve status/body for the SDK's normal error handling. }; const soter = new Soter({ fetch: strictGuardFetch, apiKey: process.env.SOTER_API_KEY, projectId: process.env.SOTER_PROJECT_ID, }); export const runtime = "nodejs"; export async function POST(req: Request) { let body: unknown; try { body = await req.json(); } catch { return Response.json({ error: "Invalid JSON", blocked: true }, { status: 400 }); } if (!body || typeof body !== "object" || Array.isArray(body) || !("message" in body) || typeof body.message !== "string" || !body.message.trim() || body.message.length > 8000) { return Response.json({ error: "message must contain 1–8000 characters", blocked: true }, { status: 400 }); } // Authenticate and rate-limit in your application before this flow. try { const input = await soter.protect({ input: body.message }); if (!soter.shouldCallLLM(input)) { return Response.json({ reply: "Message withheld.", blocked: true }, { status: 403 }); } const safeMessage = input.safeText ?? input.redactedText ?? (input.action === "ALLOW" ? body.message : undefined); if (typeof safeMessage !== "string" || !safeMessage.trim()) { return Response.json({ reply: "Message withheld.", blocked: true }, { status: 503 }); } const llmReply = await callYourLLM(safeMessage); const output = await soter.guardOutput({ text: llmReply }); if (!soter.shouldCallLLM(output)) { return Response.json({ reply: "Response withheld.", blocked: true }, { status: 403 }); } const reply = output.safeText ?? output.redactedText ?? (output.action === "ALLOW" ? llmReply : undefined); if (typeof reply !== "string" || !reply.trim()) { return Response.json({ reply: "Response withheld.", blocked: true }, { status: 503 }); } return Response.json({ reply, blocked: false }); } catch { // Includes guard/network errors and model failures. Do not echo exceptions. return Response.json({ reply: "Chat temporarily unavailable.", blocked: true }, { status: 503 }); } } // Alternative app/api/chat/route.ts; do not combine with the manual POST. import { createGuardedRoute } from "@soterai/core/next"; import { myLLMCall } from "@/lib/llm"; // Your async string-returning model adapter export const runtime = "nodejs"; // Application transport policy: validate raw JSON BEFORE SDK normalization. const strictGuardFetch: typeof fetch = async (url, init) => { const response = await fetch(url, init); if (response.ok) { const raw = await response.clone().json(); const permits = ["ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"]; if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || Array.isArray(raw) || typeof raw.allowed !== "boolean" || ![...permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW"].includes(raw.action) || raw.allowed !== permits.includes(raw.action)) { throw new Error("Invalid guard verdict"); } const decision = ["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action) ? "REDACT" : raw.action; if (raw.decision !== undefined && raw.decision !== decision) { throw new Error("Inconsistent guard decision"); } if (["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action)) { const replacement = raw.safeText ?? raw.redactedText; if (typeof replacement !== "string" || !replacement.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing usable guard replacement"); } } } return response; // Preserve status/body for the SDK's normal error handling. }; const guarded = createGuardedRoute({ fetch: strictGuardFetch, apiKey: process.env.SOTER_API_KEY!, baseUrl: process.env.SOTER_BASE_URL, projectId: process.env.SOTER_PROJECT_ID, timeoutMs: 8000, retries: 0, callLLM: async (safeInput) => myLLMCall(safeInput), }); // The SDK also returns diagnostics. Project only a minimal public response. export async function POST(req: Request) { let body: unknown; try { body = await req.json(); } catch { return Response.json({ blocked: true, reply: "Invalid JSON." }, { status: 400 }); } if (!body || typeof body !== "object" || Array.isArray(body) || !("message" in body) || typeof body.message !== "string" || !body.message.trim() || body.message.length > 8000) { return Response.json({ blocked: true, reply: "Invalid message." }, { status: 400 }); } try { // Only forward validated fields; resolve identity in your application. const response = await guarded(new Request(req.url, { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ message: body.message }), })); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Guarded route failed"); const data = await response.json(); if (data.blocked !== false || typeof data.reply !== "string") { return Response.json({ blocked: true, reply: "Response withheld." }); } return Response.json({ blocked: false, reply: data.reply }); } catch { return Response.json({ blocked: true, reply: "Chat temporarily unavailable." }, { status: 503 }); } } "use server"; import { Soter } from "@soterai/core"; import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache"; import { callLLM } from "@/lib/llm"; // Your async string-returning model adapter // Application transport policy: validate raw JSON BEFORE SDK normalization. const strictGuardFetch: typeof fetch = async (url, init) => { const response = await fetch(url, init); if (response.ok) { const raw = await response.clone().json(); const permits = ["ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"]; if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || Array.isArray(raw) || typeof raw.allowed !== "boolean" || ![...permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW"].includes(raw.action) || raw.allowed !== permits.includes(raw.action)) { throw new Error("Invalid guard verdict"); } const decision = ["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action) ? "REDACT" : raw.action; if (raw.decision !== undefined && raw.decision !== decision) { throw new Error("Inconsistent guard decision"); } if (["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action)) { const replacement = raw.safeText ?? raw.redactedText; if (typeof replacement !== "string" || !replacement.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing usable guard replacement"); } } } return response; // Preserve status/body for the SDK's normal error handling. }; const soter = new Soter({ fetch: strictGuardFetch, apiKey: process.env.SOTER_API_KEY, }); export async function submitMessage(formData: FormData) { const message = formData.get("message"); if (typeof message !== "string" || !message.trim() || message.length > 8000) { return { blocked: true, error: "Enter a message of 1–8000 characters." }; } // Resolve the authenticated user and conversation before calling the SDK. try { const result = await soter.protectChat({ message, callLLM }); if (result.blocked) { return { blocked: true, error: "Message or response withheld." }; } revalidatePath("/chat"); return { blocked: false, reply: result.safeResponse }; } catch { return { blocked: true, error: "Chat temporarily unavailable." }; } } // app/chat/page.tsx "use client"; import { useState, type FormEvent } from "react"; export default function ChatPage() { const [reply, setReply] = useState(""); const [pending, setPending] = useState(false); async function handleSubmit(e: FormEvent) { e.preventDefault(); const form = new FormData(e.currentTarget); setPending(true); try { // Only your backend receives the message. Never put the API key here. const res = await fetch("/api/chat", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ message: form.get("message") }), }); if (!res.ok) { setReply("Chat unavailable or message withheld."); return; } const data = await res.json(); setReply(data.blocked === false && typeof data.reply === "string" ? data.reply : "Response withheld."); } catch { setReply("Chat temporarily unavailable. Try again later."); } finally { setPending(false); } } return (

{reply}

); } Step 1: Install Use an existing App Router application with a Node.js server runtime. The SDK package declares Node.js 18.18 or newer; your Next.js version may require a newer runtime. terminal Choose either the manual route or the helper route below. Both require your own model adapter returning a complete string, plus application authentication and abuse controls. The SDK does not call a model for you. Step 2: Environment variables Set the project key in .env.local for local development and in your deployment's server secret store. new Soter() reads these variables; the route factory requires an explicit apiKey . .env.local Never prefix a SoterAI key with NEXT_PUBLIC_ or import the server client into a Client Component. A missing key is a configuration error, not a reason to bypass the guard. Step 3: Route Handler (manual control) The route checks request JSON, guards input and waits for an output verdict before replying. Each server example includes an application-owned strictGuardFetch : it validates the raw boolean and action before SDK normalization and requires nonblank replacement text for redaction or rewrite. Only allowed === true with ALLOW , ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION or REWRITE permits continuation. Do not remove this adapter: the SDK helpers alone use permissive verdict handling and can fall back to original text. app/api/chat/route.ts Here, invalid input returns 400, a content denial returns 403, and a guard or model failure returns 503. These are application response choices, not the raw guard API's status contract. The 8,000-character cap matches the server's default text limit; align it with your deployment and also bound HTTP body size upstream. Step 4: Guarded-route helper createGuardedRoute from @soterai/core/next runs input guard → model callback → output guard. Its default input field is message ; change it with inputField when using the factory directly. app/api/chat/route.ts · alternative The unwrapped helper returns HTTP 200 for completed turns, including blocked turns, with reply , blocked , inputResult and optional outputResult . Invalid JSON or an empty message returns 400; caught errors use their status or 500. It does not sanitize every diagnostic field or exception message. The wrapper above deliberately omits those fields and withholds failed responses. Step 5: Server Actions protectChat performs both guard calls. Return an application-owned result rather than the complete guard objects. Revalidation happens only after an allowed reply. app/chat/actions.ts A server action still needs authorization. If you add userId or sessionId , derive them from a trusted session and reuse the conversation identifier across turns. Do not treat browser-supplied IDs as proof of identity. Step 6: Client component (safe pattern) The browser calls your route and renders text. It does not need a SoterAI key or the SDK. A denial or transport error never becomes an unguarded reply. app/chat/page.tsx Key points for Next.js developers Keep credentials server-side and apply authentication, per-user limits and payload validation before guard/model work. Use route handlers or server actions for the checks. Pages Router needs its own request/response adaptation; these examples use App Router. Guard the full model output before returning it. These examples buffer strings; they do not inspect tokens already streamed to the browser. RAG retrieval and tool execution need separate checks. Input/output guarding does not authorize a database read or a tool action. examples/nextjs-chatbot contains a repository example. It only proxies an input guard call; it does not implement the complete model/output flow shown here. Verify before deployment Exercise allowed, redacted, blocked and human-review verdicts; confirm denied input never reaches the model. Force an output denial and a guard timeout. Confirm neither the original completion nor an exception body reaches the browser. Check malformed JSON, missing messages, long input, model errors and missing configuration. Test your real provider adapter separately. What's next? JavaScript SDK Express.js Guide REST API ← REST API Express.js Guide → Covers App Router route handlers and server actions. Pages Router API routes work the same way but are not shown. Guarding inside a Client Component is not supported: the key would be exposed to the browser.

headings.text: Key points for Next.js developers Keep credentials server-side and apply authentication, per-user limits and payload validation before guard/model work. Use route handlers or server actions for the checks. Pages Router needs its own request/response adaptation; these examples use App Router. Guard the full model output before returning it. These examples buffer strings; they do not inspect tokens already streamed to the browser. RAG retrieval and tool execution need separate checks. Input/output guarding does not authorize a database read or a tool action. examples/nextjs-chatbot contains a repository example. It only proxies an input guard call; it does not implement the complete model/output flow shown here. Verify before deployment Exercise allowed, redacted, blocked and human-review verdicts; confirm denied input never reaches the model. Force an output denial and a guard timeout. Confirm neither the original completion nor an exception body reaches the browser. Check malformed JSON, missing messages, long input, model errors and missing configuration. Test your real provider adapter separately.

pages.summary: Input and output guard middleware for existing Express chat routes.
pages.body: npm install @soterai/core express # Inject into the server process; the SDK does not load .env files. SOTER_API_KEY=replace_with_your_project_key SOTER_BASE_URL=https://api.soterai.in # Optional metadata; authentication still selects the API key's project. SOTER_PROJECT_ID= // server.js (ES module); use your application's existing listener. import express from "express"; import { Soter } from "@soterai/core"; import { callLLM } from "./llm.js"; // Your adapter: (text) => Promise<string> // Application transport policy: validate raw JSON BEFORE SDK normalization. const strictGuardFetch = async (url, init) => { const response = await fetch(url, init); if (response.ok) { const raw = await response.clone().json(); const permits = ["ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"]; if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || Array.isArray(raw) || typeof raw.allowed !== "boolean" || ![...permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW"].includes(raw.action) || raw.allowed !== permits.includes(raw.action)) { throw new Error("Invalid guard verdict"); } const decision = ["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action) ? "REDACT" : raw.action; if (raw.decision !== undefined && raw.decision !== decision) { throw new Error("Inconsistent guard decision"); } if (["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action)) { const replacement = raw.safeText ?? raw.redactedText; if (typeof replacement !== "string" || !replacement.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing usable guard replacement"); } } } return response; // Preserve status/body for the SDK's normal error handling. }; const app = express(); app.use(express.json({ limit: "32kb" })); const soter = new Soter({ timeoutMs: 8000, retries: 0, fetch: strictGuardFetch }); app.post("/chat", async (req, res, next) => { const message = req.body?.message; if (typeof message !== "string" || !message.trim() || message.length > 8000) { return res.status(400).json({ blocked: true, reply: "Invalid message." }); } try { const input = await soter.protect({ input: message }); if (!soter.shouldCallLLM(input)) { return res.status(403).json({ blocked: true, reply: "Message withheld." }); } const safeInput = input.safeText ?? input.redactedText ?? (input.action === "ALLOW" ? message : undefined); if (typeof safeInput !== "string" || !safeInput.trim()) { throw new Error("No usable input after guarding"); } const llmReply = await callLLM(safeInput); const output = await soter.guardOutput({ text: llmReply }); if (!soter.shouldCallLLM(output)) { return res.status(403).json({ blocked: true, reply: "Response withheld." }); } const reply = output.safeText ?? output.redactedText ?? (output.action === "ALLOW" ? llmReply : undefined); if (typeof reply !== "string" || !reply.trim()) { throw new Error("No usable output after guarding"); } return res.json({ blocked: false, reply }); } catch (error) { next(error); // Express 4 and 5: forward async failures explicitly. } }); // Keep all four parameters: Express identifies error handlers by arity. app.use((error, req, res, next) => { const status = error?.type === "entity.parse.failed" ? 400 : error?.type === "entity.too.large" ? 413 : 503; res.status(status).json({ blocked: true, reply: "Chat unavailable or invalid request." }); }); export default app; // Alternative server.js; do not register alongside the manual /chat route. import express from "express"; import { soterInputMiddleware, soterOutputMiddleware } from "@soterai/core/express"; import { callLLM } from "./llm.js"; // Application transport policy: validate raw JSON BEFORE SDK normalization. const strictGuardFetch = async (url, init) => { const response = await fetch(url, init); if (response.ok) { const raw = await response.clone().json(); const permits = ["ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"]; if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || Array.isArray(raw) || typeof raw.allowed !== "boolean" || ![...permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW"].includes(raw.action) || raw.allowed !== permits.includes(raw.action)) { throw new Error("Invalid guard verdict"); } const decision = ["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action) ? "REDACT" : raw.action; if (raw.decision !== undefined && raw.decision !== decision) { throw new Error("Inconsistent guard decision"); } if (["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action)) { const replacement = raw.safeText ?? raw.redactedText; if (typeof replacement !== "string" || !replacement.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing usable guard replacement"); } } if (!raw.allowed) { // Middleware sends denials before later application handlers run. // Never let guard-supplied text or diagnostics become the refusal. return new Response(JSON.stringify({ allowed: false, action: raw.action, decision, safeText: "Response withheld.", }), { status: response.status, headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }); } } return response; // Preserve permitted replies and normal SDK error handling. }; const app = express(); app.use(express.json({ limit: "32kb" })); const apiKey = process.env.SOTER_API_KEY; if (!apiKey) throw new Error("Set SOTER_API_KEY on the server"); const options = { fetch: strictGuardFetch, apiKey, baseUrl: process.env.SOTER_BASE_URL, projectId: process.env.SOTER_PROJECT_ID, timeoutMs: 8000, retries: 0, }; app.post( "/chat", (req, res, next) => { if (typeof req.body?.message !== "string" || !req.body.message.trim() || req.body.message.length > 8000) { return res.status(400).json({ blocked: true, reply: "Invalid message." }); } next(); }, soterInputMiddleware({ ...options, field: "message", rewriteBody: true }), async (req, res, next) => { try { // The input middleware has replaced message with safe/redacted text. res.locals.aiResponse = await callLLM(req.body.message); next(); // Do not send JSON yet: output inspection comes next. } catch (error) { next(error); } }, soterOutputMiddleware({ ...options, field: "aiResponse", rewriteBody: true }), (req, res) => res.json({ blocked: false, reply: res.locals.aiResponse }), ); app.use((error, req, res, next) => { const status = error?.type === "entity.parse.failed" ? 400 : error?.type === "entity.too.large" ? 413 : 503; res.status(status).json({ blocked: true, reply: "Chat unavailable or invalid request." }); }); export default app; Step 1: Install Use a server-side Express application and Node.js 18.18 or newer for the SDK. Check your Express version's runtime requirements separately. The examples use ES modules; keep your existing server bootstrap and supply a model adapter that returns a complete string. terminal server environment Load local environment files through your application bootstrap or deployment tooling. Keep the key out of browser bundles, source control and logs. Neither middleware authenticates the people using your chat endpoint. Step 2: Basic usage Validate the message, guard input, call the model with permitted text and guard its output before serialization. Both examples include an application-owned strictGuardFetch before SDK normalization: raw allowed must be boolean, the action and optional decision must agree, and redaction/rewrite must supply nonblank replacement text. Only an explicit true grant with an allowlisted action continues. Keep this adapter on both middleware calls; the SDK fallback alone can reuse original text. server.js · manual route The manual route chooses 403 for a content denial and 503 for operational failure. The 8,000-character bound matches the guard server's default; the 32 KB parser limit is an independent application limit. Tune both for your deployment rather than removing validation. If you pass context.userId or context.sessionId to protect , derive them from authenticated application state. Express does not create req.user or req.session automatically. Pass the same conversation ID to output checks when you need correlation. Step 3: Use input and output middleware Order matters: parse and validate → input middleware → model → output middleware → response. These middleware functions inspect specific text fields; they do not intercept every res.json call. server.js · middleware alternative soterInputMiddleware reads req.body.message by default and rewrites that field when rewriteBody is true, the default. soterOutputMiddleware reads res.locals.aiResponse , falling back to the same field on the request body. It rewrites res.locals ; put model output there, not in a client-controlled field. Both expose results on req.soter.inputResult / outputResult , with legacy req.cyberrakshak aliases. Keep full diagnostics off the public response. A missing text field returns 400. A block or human-review verdict ends the middleware chain with HTTP 200 and blocked: true . Guard errors go to next(error) ; the final handler above withholds the response. The input middleware forwards body metadata, not user/session IDs. For trusted identity context on both checks, use the manual flow. Example project examples/express-chatbot is a historical starter. Its named createExpressMiddleware import is not exported by the current @soterai/core/express entry point. Use the two current middleware exports shown above, or the Soter.createExpressMiddleware instance method documented in the JavaScript SDK guide. Verify the application boundary Check allowed and redacted messages, blocked input, blocked output and human review. Assert that the model never runs on denied input. Simulate a timeout or non-2xx guard response. Confirm the error handler runs and does not echo the model text, request body or exception details. Add user authentication, per-user/IP abuse controls and output encoding. RAG authorization and tool permissions remain separate application responsibilities. These examples buffer complete strings. WebSocket and SSE paths need their own pre-release output gate; inspecting text after streaming cannot retract it. What's next? JavaScript SDK FastAPI Guide ← Next.js Guide FastAPI Guide → Assumes an existing Express app with a chat route. It is not an Express tutorial. Does not cover WebSocket or Server-Sent Event streaming, where the output guard needs to buffer before it can decide.

pages.title: FastAPI
pages.summary: Async Python routes with Pydantic request and response models.
pages.body: pip install "soter[fastapi]" # For the async variant below, also install the async extra: pip install "soter[fastapi,async]" # Set in your server process or secret manager before starting the app. SOTER_API_KEY=replace_with_your_project_key # Optional; this is the SDK's default origin. SOTER_BASE_URL=https://api.soterai.in # main.py from fastapi import FastAPI from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, StrictStr from soter import Soter, SoterError from soter.fastapi import create_chat_route from your_app.llm import my_llm_call # Your synchronous (str) -> str adapter import json import requests # Application transport policy: inspect raw JSON before GuardResult coercion. class StrictSession(requests.Session): def post(self, *args, **kwargs): response = super().post(*args, **kwargs) if response.status_code < 400: try: raw = json.loads(response.text) except ValueError as exc: raise SoterError("Invalid guard JSON") from exc permits = ("ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE") if (not isinstance(raw, dict) or type(raw.get("allowed")) is not bool or raw.get("action") not in (*permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW") or raw["allowed"] is not (raw["action"] in permits)): raise SoterError("Invalid guard verdict") action = raw["action"] decision = "REDACT" if action in permits[1:] else action if raw.get("decision", decision) != decision: raise SoterError("Inconsistent guard decision") if action in permits[1:]: replacement = raw.get("safeText", raw.get("safe_text")) if replacement is None: replacement = raw.get("redactedText", raw.get("redacted_text")) if not isinstance(replacement, str) or not replacement.strip(): raise SoterError("Missing usable guard replacement") return response app = FastAPI() guard = Soter(timeout=8.0, max_retries=0, session=StrictSession()) guarded_chat = create_chat_route(guard, call_llm=my_llm_call) class ChatRequest(BaseModel): message: StrictStr = Field(min_length=1, max_length=8000) @app.post("/chat") def chat(req: ChatRequest): if not req.message.strip(): return JSONResponse(status_code=422, content={"blocked": True, "reply": "Invalid message."}) try: # The adapter's result is a camelCase dictionary, including diagnostics. result = guarded_chat({"message": req.message}) if result["blocked"]: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Message or response withheld."} return {"blocked": False, "reply": result["safeResponse"]} except SoterError: return JSONResponse(status_code=503, content={"blocked": True, "reply": "Guard temporarily unavailable."}) except Exception: return JSONResponse(status_code=502, content={"blocked": True, "reply": "Model request failed."}) # Alternative main.py: call protect_chat directly. from fastapi import FastAPI from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, StrictStr from soter import Soter, SoterError from your_app.llm import my_llm_call import json import requests # Application transport policy: inspect raw JSON before GuardResult coercion. class StrictSession(requests.Session): def post(self, *args, **kwargs): response = super().post(*args, **kwargs) if response.status_code < 400: try: raw = json.loads(response.text) except ValueError as exc: raise SoterError("Invalid guard JSON") from exc permits = ("ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE") if (not isinstance(raw, dict) or type(raw.get("allowed")) is not bool or raw.get("action") not in (*permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW") or raw["allowed"] is not (raw["action"] in permits)): raise SoterError("Invalid guard verdict") action = raw["action"] decision = "REDACT" if action in permits[1:] else action if raw.get("decision", decision) != decision: raise SoterError("Inconsistent guard decision") if action in permits[1:]: replacement = raw.get("safeText", raw.get("safe_text")) if replacement is None: replacement = raw.get("redactedText", raw.get("redacted_text")) if not isinstance(replacement, str) or not replacement.strip(): raise SoterError("Missing usable guard replacement") return response app = FastAPI() guard = Soter(timeout=8.0, max_retries=0, session=StrictSession()) class ChatRequest(BaseModel): message: StrictStr = Field(min_length=1, max_length=8000) @app.post("/chat") def chat(req: ChatRequest): if not req.message.strip(): return JSONResponse(status_code=422, content={"blocked": True, "reply": "Invalid message."}) try: result = guard.protect_chat(message=req.message, call_llm=my_llm_call) if result.blocked: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Message or response withheld."} return {"blocked": False, "reply": result.safe_response} except SoterError: return JSONResponse(status_code=503, content={"blocked": True, "reply": "Guard temporarily unavailable."}) except Exception: return JSONResponse(status_code=502, content={"blocked": True, "reply": "Model request failed."}) # Alternative main.py: install soter[fastapi,async]. from contextlib import asynccontextmanager from fastapi import FastAPI from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, StrictStr from soter import AsyncSoter, SoterError from your_app.llm import my_async_llm_call # Your async (str) -> str adapter import json import httpx # Application transport policy: inspect raw JSON before GuardResult coercion. class StrictAsyncClient(httpx.AsyncClient): async def post(self, *args, **kwargs): response = await super().post(*args, **kwargs) if response.status_code < 400: try: raw = json.loads(response.text) except ValueError as exc: raise SoterError("Invalid guard JSON") from exc permits = ("ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE") if (not isinstance(raw, dict) or type(raw.get("allowed")) is not bool or raw.get("action") not in (*permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW") or raw["allowed"] is not (raw["action"] in permits)): raise SoterError("Invalid guard verdict") action = raw["action"] decision = "REDACT" if action in permits[1:] else action if raw.get("decision", decision) != decision: raise SoterError("Inconsistent guard decision") if action in permits[1:]: replacement = raw.get("safeText", raw.get("safe_text")) if replacement is None: replacement = raw.get("redactedText", raw.get("redacted_text")) if not isinstance(replacement, str) or not replacement.strip(): raise SoterError("Missing usable guard replacement") return response http_client = StrictAsyncClient() guard = AsyncSoter(timeout=8.0, max_retries=0, client=http_client) @asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app: FastAPI): try: yield finally: await http_client.aclose() # This application owns the injected client. app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan) class ChatRequest(BaseModel): message: StrictStr = Field(min_length=1, max_length=8000) @app.post("/chat") async def chat(req: ChatRequest): if not req.message.strip(): return JSONResponse(status_code=422, content={"blocked": True, "reply": "Invalid message."}) try: result = await guard.protect_chat(message=req.message, call_llm=my_async_llm_call) if result.blocked: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Message or response withheld."} return {"blocked": False, "reply": result.safe_response} except SoterError: return JSONResponse(status_code=503, content={"blocked": True, "reply": "Guard temporarily unavailable."}) except Exception: return JSONResponse(status_code=502, content={"blocked": True, "reply": "Model request failed."}) Step 1: Install The local Python distribution is soter and declares Python 3.9 or newer. Use your application's environment; the fastapi extra adds FastAPI, while async adds HTTPX. An ASGI server such as Uvicorn is a separate dependency. terminal server environment Soter() reads SOTER_API_KEY and SOTER_BASE_URL from the process environment. It does not load a .env file. A missing key raises SoterConfigError . The Python constructor does not accept project_id ; the API key selects its project. Choose one of the three route implementations below and supply the named model adapter. Configure user authentication, authorization and request/body limits before exposing /chat . These examples do not provide those controls. Step 2: Quickstart with the route adapter create_chat_route wraps protect_chat , synchronously for Soter or asynchronously for AsyncSoter . Each example supplies an application-owned strict HTTP adapter before SDK normalization: raw allowed must be boolean and agree with an allowlisted action; redaction/rewrite requires nonblank replacement text. This prevents truthy strings and the SDK's original-text fallback from permitting continuation. Keep the adapter as well as Pydantic validation and the public-response wrapper. main.py · route adapter You can mount the unwrapped handler with app.add_api_route("/chat", create_chat_route(guard, call_llm=my_llm_call), methods=["POST"]) . Its input is a dictionary with message , optional userId and sessionId ; the field names are configurable. It does not enforce the schema or translate SDK exceptions shown above. The unwrapped result uses camelCase: safeResponse , inputGuard , outputGuard and llmCalled . Full results are diagnostic data, not a sanitized public-response format. Step 3: Manual guarding (more control) Calling protect_chat directly returns a ProtectChatResult object. Its Python attributes use snake_case. to_dict() produces camelCase keys and includes guard details; the example intentionally does not serialize that entire object. main.py · direct orchestration The SDK skips the model on a denied or human-review input. It guards the completed model string before returning. To add trusted correlation, pass user_id and session_id resolved by your server, not copied from an unauthenticated browser payload. Step 4: Async support AsyncSoter supports awaitable callbacks and exposes aclose() for its owned HTTP client. Use an async model adapter for network work; passing a blocking synchronous function does not move it into a worker thread. main.py · async alternative If you inject an httpx.AsyncClient , you own its cleanup. Keep the sync client in a synchronous FastAPI handler; do not run its blocking HTTP requests directly inside an async endpoint. Response and failure policy These wrappers return 200 for completed turns, including a fixed reply with blocked: true . Invalid fields return 422, SDK failures return 503, and model exceptions return 502. The guard API's 400, 401/403 and 429 become typed SDK exceptions; other HTTP failures raise SoterError . Python max_retries retries transport exceptions, not HTTP 429/5xx responses. Timeout values are seconds. Use SoterRateLimitError.retry_after when designing backoff. Keep unavailable requests withheld; do not fall back to the original model text. The 8,000-character validation follows the server default. The server can configure a different limit; align the application schema and bound HTTP body size at the ingress. These are complete-string examples. Background tasks and streaming need their own mechanism to prevent release before a verdict. Verify the integration Use synthetic messages to test allow, redaction, block and human review. Count model calls to prove denied input stops early. Force a guard timeout and an output denial; inspect the HTTP response for leaked completion or diagnostic fields. Test the real model adapter separately from these control-flow checks. What's next? Python SDK Guide RAG/LangChain ← Express.js Guide Python SDK → Assumes a working FastAPI app. Does not cover deployment, ASGI server tuning, or dependency injection patterns. Background-task guarding is not shown; a rejected result must still reach the caller.

pages.summary: Inspect retrieved context and citations before they reach the model.
pages.body: # Python: the wrappers do not install LangChain or LlamaIndex for you. pip install soter # TypeScript / Node.js: npm install @soterai/core from soter import Soter, SoterError from soter.langchain import protect_langchain_chain from your_app.rag import my_chain # Application transport policy: inspect raw JSON before GuardResult coercion. class StrictSession(requests.Session): def post(self, *args, **kwargs): response = super().post(*args, **kwargs) if response.status_code < 400: try: raw = json.loads(response.text) except ValueError as exc: raise SoterError("Invalid guard JSON") from exc permits = ("ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE") if (not isinstance(raw, dict) or type(raw.get("allowed")) is not bool or raw.get("action") not in (*permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW") or raw["allowed"] is not (raw["action"] in permits)): raise SoterError("Invalid guard verdict") action = raw["action"] decision = "REDACT" if action in permits[1:] else action if raw.get("decision", decision) != decision: raise SoterError("Inconsistent guard decision") if action in permits[1:]: replacement = raw.get("safeText", raw.get("safe_text")) if replacement is None: replacement = raw.get("redactedText", raw.get("redacted_text")) if not isinstance(replacement, str) or not replacement.strip(): raise SoterError("Missing usable guard replacement") return response guard = Soter(timeout=8.0, max_retries=0, session=StrictSession()) # principal_id must come from your authenticated application session. def answer_rag(query: str, principal_id: str): if not isinstance(query, str) or not query.strip() or len(query) > 8000: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Invalid query."} def retrieve(safe_query): # Enforce tenant/document permissions in this application adapter. docs = retrieve_authorized(safe_query, principal_id) return [RagSource(id=doc["id"], text=doc["text"], citation=doc.get("url")) for doc in docs] def call_llm(payload): # The SDK calls this even when all chunks were excluded. if not payload["sources"]: raise ValueError("No eligible sources") reply = generate_answer(payload["safeQuery"], payload["safeContext"]) if not isinstance(reply, str): raise TypeError("The model adapter must return text") return reply try: result = guard.protect_rag(query=query, retrieve=retrieve, call_llm=call_llm) if result.blocked: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Message or response withheld."} return {"blocked": False, "reply": result.safe_response} except SoterError: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Guard temporarily unavailable."} except Exception: # Includes empty eligible context, retrieval and generation failures. return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Unable to answer from eligible sources."} import { Soter } from "@soterai/core"; import { retrieveAuthorized, generateAnswer } from "./rag"; // Your application adapters // Application transport policy: validate raw JSON BEFORE SDK normalization. const strictGuardFetch: typeof fetch = async (url, init) => { const response = await fetch(url, init); if (response.ok) { const raw = await response.clone().json(); const permits = ["ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"]; if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || Array.isArray(raw) || typeof raw.allowed !== "boolean" || ![...permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW"].includes(raw.action) || raw.allowed !== permits.includes(raw.action)) { throw new Error("Invalid guard verdict"); } const decision = ["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action) ? "REDACT" : raw.action; if (raw.decision !== undefined && raw.decision !== decision) { throw new Error("Inconsistent guard decision"); } if (["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action)) { const replacement = raw.safeText ?? raw.redactedText; if (typeof replacement !== "string" || !replacement.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing usable guard replacement"); } } } return response; // Preserve status/body for the SDK's normal error handling. }; const soter = new Soter({ timeoutMs: 8000, retries: 0, fetch: strictGuardFetch }); export async function answerRag(userQuery: string, principalId: string) { if (typeof userQuery !== "string" || !userQuery.trim() || userQuery.length > 8000) { return { blocked: true, reply: "Invalid query." }; } try { const result = await soter.protectRag({ query: userQuery, retrieve: async (safeQuery) => { // principalId is trusted server state. default False. ) def ask_index(question: str): if not isinstance(question, str) or not question.strip() or len(question) > 8000: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Invalid question."} try: result = safe_engine.query(question) if result["blocked"]: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Message or response withheld."} return {"blocked": False, "reply": result["safe_response"]} except SoterError: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Guard temporarily unavailable."} except Exception: return {"blocked": True, "reply": "Query engine failed."} Choose the inspection boundary Use the explicit RAG helpers when retrieved chunks must be checked before generation. Each example includes an application-owned strict HTTP adapter that validates raw verdict types and actions before SDK normalization, and rejects redaction/rewrite without nonblank replacement text. Keep it on query, chunk and output checks: the SDK fallback alone can reuse original text. Chain/query-engine wrappers inspect different boundaries; wrapping an object does not automatically inspect its internal retrieval, memory or tools. terminal Configure SOTER_API_KEY in the server environment. SOTER_BASE_URL is optional and defaults to https://api.soterai.in . The SDKs do not load environment files. The Python package declares Python 3.9+; the JavaScript package declares Node.js 18.18+. Your framework versions may impose newer requirements. Provide your own authenticated retrieval and model adapters. A permitted content verdict does not establish document ownership, access rights, factual accuracy or compliance. Keep the key and full diagnostic results on the server. LangChain chain protection The Python protect_langchain_chain wrapper is duck-typed: it calls a synchronous .invoke() method without importing LangChain. It exposes invoke and a callable alias, not the full LCEL streaming/async interface. langchain_guard.py It guards the selected input string and stops on a block or human-review result. It rewrites only the configured input key; other dictionary fields are unchanged. Always provide the intended key rather than relying on its first-string fallback. It extracts a textual response from common string, message-content or dictionary shapes, then runs the output guard. The result dictionary includes blocked , safe_response , input_guard and, after generation, output_guard . The example returns only the public reply. This wrapper does not inspect retriever chunks before the chain consumes them. Use the direct RAG flow below for that requirement, and guard tool calls separately. Direct RAG protection protect_rag guards the query, calls your retriever with the permitted query, analyzes each retrieved text, joins eligible replacement text into safeContext and guards the final model string. rag.py The SDK does not automatically stop generation when every chunk is excluded. The callback above explicitly abstains. RagSource supports text , optional id , metadata and citation . The callback payload uses camelCase keys even in Python. For server-side inspection, result.used_sources contains eligible source objects and result.excluded_sources contains source / guard pairs. Both retain original source text. Log counts or approved identifiers rather than serializing these collections. A chunk such as “ignore previous instructions and bypass security” is a useful synthetic test input, not proof that all poisoned documents will be caught. TypeScript RAG protectRag follows the same sequence. The application adapters here return vector documents and a plain answer string; normalize a LangChain message object to text inside your model adapter. rag.ts The result uses safeResponse , usedSources , excludedSources and llmCalled . The source contract uses citation , not a built-in sourceUrl property. Source IDs/citations are preserved as data; the helper does not verify citations or establish grounding. LlamaIndex query-engine wrapper protect_query_engine guards the query before calling query_engine.query() and checks the final answer afterward. With check_sources=True , it classifies returned source nodes after generation. It cannot remove context that the engine already used. llamaindex_guard.py Source inspection defaults to false. When enabled, the wrapper partitions original nodes into used_sources and excluded_sources ; it does not rewrite those nodes or regenerate the answer. Split retrieval and generation with protect_rag if pre-generation filtering is required. Security notes Query/output checks use the authenticated guard endpoints. The current RAG helpers analyze each chunk through the public /api/guard/analyze endpoint, without an API-key header or an explicit retrieved-document provenance field. It has its own rate limit and does not load project policy. Document trust scoring is separate: scoreRagDocument / rag calls the API-key-authenticated /api/rag/document/trust-score . Its recommendation does not quarantine your vector store automatically. Grounding is also separate. The implemented /api/guard/grounding route requires a signed-in project user with rag:read permission and resolves stored chunk IDs. It is not the same public API-key contract as input/output guarding, and these SDK helpers do not call it. Enforce tenant/principal access before returning documents from your retriever, including permission changes and revocation. SoterAI's own RAG authorization checks do not automatically apply to an external vector database. Send only the eligible safeContext to generation. Keep original source objects and diagnostics away from prompts, logs and browser responses unless separately reviewed. Bound query and chunk sizes to the server's configured text limit, and budget one scan per chunk. A failed chunk scan must not become permission to use the original context. These checks can produce false positives and false negatives. They do not guarantee protection against poisoned retrieval, factual accuracy or confidential-data leakage. Verify with synthetic retrieval Test denied queries, mixed eligible/excluded chunks, no eligible sources, redacted text, guard failures and blocked output. Observe which bytes reach the model. Verify tenant isolation and source freshness in your own retriever, and test the separate grounding/approval workflow only under its actual authentication contract. What's next? Document trust scoring reduces the impact of poisoned context; it does not guarantee that poisoned context is caught.

pages.title: Any chatbot or agent
pages.summary: The universal pattern for when no framework-specific guide applies.
pages.body: # Set in the server environment, not the browser or mobile application. SOTER_API_KEY=replace_with_your_project_key # Optional; the SDK uses this origin by default. SOTER_BASE_URL=https://api.soterai.in import { Soter, type SoterContext } from "@soterai/core"; import { callLLM } from "./llm"; // Your adapter: (text) => Promise<string> // Application transport policy: validate raw JSON BEFORE SDK normalization. const strictGuardFetch: typeof fetch = async (url, init) => { const response = await fetch(url, init); if (response.ok) { const raw = await response.clone().json(); const permits = ["ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"]; if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || Array.isArray(raw) || typeof raw.allowed !== "boolean" || ![...permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW"].includes(raw.action) || raw.allowed !== permits.includes(raw.action)) { throw new Error("Invalid guard verdict"); } const decision = ["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action) ? "REDACT" : raw.action; if (raw.decision !== undefined && raw.decision !== decision) { throw new Error("Inconsistent guard decision"); } if (["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action)) { const replacement = raw.safeText ?? raw.redactedText; if (typeof replacement !== "string" || !replacement.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing usable guard replacement"); } } } return response; // Preserve status/body for the SDK's normal error handling. }; const soter = new Soter({ timeoutMs: 8000, retries: 0, fetch: strictGuardFetch }); // Call from your authenticated transport; context comes from server state. export async function chat(userMessage: string, context: SoterContext = {}) { if (typeof userMessage !== "string" || !userMessage.trim() || userMessage.length > 8000) { return { blocked: true, reply: "Invalid message." }; } try { const input = await soter.protect({ input: userMessage, context }); if (!soter.shouldCallLLM(input)) { return { blocked: true, reply: "Message withheld." }; } const safeInput = input.safeText ?? input.redactedText ?? (input.action === "ALLOW" ? userMessage : undefined); if (typeof safeInput !== "string" || !safeInput.trim()) { return { blocked: true, reply: "Message withheld." }; } const llmReply = await callLLM(safeInput); const output = await soter.guardOutput({ text: llmReply, userId: context.userId, sessionId: context.sessionId, }); if (!soter.shouldCallLLM(output)) { return { blocked: true, reply: "Response withheld." }; } const reply = output.safeText ?? output.redactedText ?? (output.action === "ALLOW" ? llmReply : undefined); return typeof reply === "string" && reply.trim() ? { blocked: false, reply } : { blocked: true, reply: "Response withheld." }; } catch { return { blocked: true, reply: "Chat temporarily unavailable." }; } } import { Soter, createAgentFirewallClient } from "@soterai/core"; import { callTool } from "./tools"; // Your fixed-destination ticket adapter const apiKey = process.env.SOTER_API_KEY; if (!apiKey) throw new Error("Set SOTER_API_KEY on the server"); const options = { apiKey, baseUrl: process.env.SOTER_BASE_URL, timeoutMs: 8000, retries: 0 }; // Application transport policy: validate raw JSON BEFORE SDK normalization. const strictGuardFetch: typeof fetch = async (url, init) => { const response = await fetch(url, init); if (response.ok) { const raw = await response.clone().json(); const permits = ["ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"]; if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || Array.isArray(raw) || typeof raw.allowed !== "boolean" || ![...permits, "BLOCK", "HUMAN_REVIEW"].includes(raw.action) || raw.allowed !== permits.includes(raw.action)) { throw new Error("Invalid guard verdict"); } const decision = ["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action) ? "REDACT" : raw.action; if (raw.decision !== undefined && raw.decision !== decision) { throw new Error("Inconsistent guard decision"); } if (["ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(raw.action)) { const replacement = raw.safeText ?? raw.redactedText; if (typeof replacement !== "string" || !replacement.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing usable guard replacement"); } } } return response; // Preserve status/body for the SDK's normal error handling. }; const soter = new Soter({ ...options, fetch: strictGuardFetch }); const firewall = createAgentFirewallClient(options); // One isolated agent action. Reuse a server-bound session for a longer run. export async function runAgentAction(ticketPayload: string) { if (typeof ticketPayload !== "string" || !ticketPayload.trim() || ticketPayload.length > 20000) { return { blocked: true, reply: "Invalid ticket content." }; } try { const session = await firewall.startAgentSession({ agentName: "support-bot", agentType: "chatbot", }); const action = await firewall.checkAgentAction({ sessionId: session.sessionId, agentName: "support-bot", tool: "api.call", action: "post_ticket", target: "https://tickets.example.test/api/tickets", // Replace with your allowlisted target. content: ticketPayload, // The API accepts a string, not an arbitrary object. destination: "external", riskContext: { externalDestination: true, canModifyData: true, canSendMessage: true }, }); // A write cannot satisfy READ_ONLY. This example has no sandbox or approval UI. if (action.decision !== "ALLOW" && action.decision !== "REDACT") { return { blocked: true, reply: "Action withheld or awaiting review." }; } const content = action.decision === "REDACT" ? action.safeContent : action.safeContent ?? ticketPayload; if (typeof content !== "string" || !content.trim()) { return { blocked: true, reply: "Action withheld." }; } // Execute this exact checked action/target with this content only. const toolResult = await callTool(content); const output = await soter.guardOutput({ text: toolResult, sessionId: session.sessionId }); if (!soter.shouldCallLLM(output)) { return { blocked: true, reply: "Tool response withheld." }; } const reply = output.safeText ?? output.redactedText ?? (output.action === "ALLOW" ? toolResult : undefined); return typeof reply === "string" && reply.trim() ? { blocked: false, reply } : { blocked: true, reply: "Tool response withheld." }; } catch { // A tool timeout can leave an uncertain side effect. Do not auto-retry the write. return { blocked: true, reply: "Action could not be completed safely." }; } } Step 1: Install the SDK Use this pattern when your stack has no framework-specific guide. The SDK declares Node.js 18.18 or newer. You supply the transport, authenticated session, model adapter and tool executor. terminal npm install @soterai/core server environment Soter reads the process environment; it does not load environment files. createAgentFirewallClient requires explicit client options. Missing configuration must stop startup rather than enable an unguarded fallback. Step 2: Basic chatbot pattern Gate the model call on the input verdict, then gate the public reply on the output verdict. Both examples use an application-owned strictGuardFetch for text guards before SDK normalization: only a raw boolean true with ALLOW , ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION or REWRITE permits continuation, and transformed results require nonblank replacement text. BLOCK , HUMAN_REVIEW , malformed grants and inconsistent decisions stop. The agent firewall keeps its separate decision contract. chatbot.ts Pass context.userId and a stable context.sessionId from trusted application state. These fields correlate activity; they do not authenticate an end user. The example's 8,000-character cap matches the guard server default and can be made stricter by your application. Step 3: Agent with tool firewall Text guarding does not authorize tools. Check the proposed action immediately before executing it, using the real destination, target and side-effect flags. The authenticated endpoints are /api/agent/session/start and /api/agent/action/check . agent-firewall.ts Replace the reserved example target and implement callTool so it uses only that checked destination and content. An output denial hides the tool result; it cannot undo a ticket already created. Never let a model switch the target or arguments after approval. Handle each tool decision ALLOW / REDACT Execute only the checked action. For REDACT, require and use safeContent ; do not fall back to the original payload when it is absent. BLOCK / ASK_APPROVAL Stop. An approval prompt is not approval. Keep the approval token and reviewed action in a trusted server workflow; an authorized reviewer must resolve the request before the exact reviewed action can run. READ_ONLY / SANDBOX_ONLY Use an executor that actually enforces the restriction, or stop. The sample stops because its ticket-writing executor is neither read-only nor sandboxed. Unknown result / request failure Withhold the action and return an application-owned error. Step 1: Install the plugin The repository ships SoterAI Guard 0.1.0 in integrations/wordpress-plugin/soter-guard . It declares WordPress 5.8+ and PHP 7.4+. It provides PHP helpers and local REST proxies; it does not install a chatbot or automatically intercept another plugin's model calls. Copy that soter-guard folder into wp-content/plugins/ , or upload the packaged zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin . Activate SoterAI Guard from the Plugins page. Package a zip from the repo root: terminal npm run package:wordpress # produces dist/soter-guard.zip Step 2: Configure settings Navigate to Settings → SoterAI Guard to configure: Setting Notes API Base URL HTTPS origin; defaults to https://api.soterai.in. The client appends /api/guard/input or /api/guard/output. API Key Stored in WordPress options and masked in the admin form. Protect database access and backups; masking is not encryption. Project ID Optional metadata only. The API key determines the authorized project. Enable Input Guard Enables the input REST proxy check; off passes text through. PHP helpers call the API independently of this toggle. Enable Output Guard Enables the output REST proxy check; off passes text through. PHP helpers call the API independently of this toggle. Enable Security Badge Stored preference; this package's shortcode rendering uses its show_badge attribute instead. Block message Shown when a request is blocked Public rate limit Transient-based limit shared by both proxies, keyed by REMOTE_ADDR. Default 30; configurable from 1 to 240. Save settings before using Test connection . It sends a fixed test message to the authenticated input endpoint; it does not verify your chatbot's routing. Settings and the test action require the WordPress manage_options capability and a nonce. Step 3: Use shortcodes The first shortcode emits route URLs and a wp_rest nonce in .soter-guard-config , plus a badge by default. Use the second form to hide the badge. The badge-only shortcode performs no guarding. wordpress editor Step 4: PHP integration (server-side) Call both PHP helpers inside the server handler that owns generation and delivery. This example withholds both input and output on a reported error or denial, including HUMAN_REVIEW. my_chatbot_generate is your own model adapter, not a plugin function. functions.php The shipped client is not a strict response-schema validator: a malformed successful API response can normalize to ALLOW. If you require fail-closed validation of every upstream response, add that validation in your server integration rather than treating this helper as a complete enforcement boundary. Escape the chosen reply for its final HTML context, or return it through WordPress JSON helpers. Step 5: Frontend via local proxy The frontend JavaScript calls the local WordPress REST route, never the SoterAI API directly. Both /wp-json/soter/v1/guard-input and /wp-json/soter/v1/guard-output accept POST JSON with text . Use the shortcode URLs rather than hard-coding the site root, especially for WordPress installed in a subdirectory. The public routes check a nonce and a best-effort per-IP limit, not visitor authentication. Browser checks can be bypassed, and the public response omits the PHP error flag. Use this only for UI feedback; keep final input/output enforcement in PHP and handle rejected checks in your UI. frontend.js Troubleshooting Auth error on test Check the saved key and HTTPS base URL. Blank or all-asterisk key submissions preserve the existing key; enter a new value only when replacing it. Base URL rejected Must start with https:// 403 from proxy Check the shortcode's current nonce. Cached or stale page markup may require a refreshed page; never expose the API key as a workaround. 429 from proxy The local transient limit is exhausted. Review traffic and proxy/IP behavior before raising the configured cap. Guard unreachable or upstream error The client passes original text through for both directions on transport errors and non-429 HTTP errors, with error=true. Upstream 429 is normalized to BLOCK. Check error in PHP; the local proxy hides it and can still return HTTP 200. What's next? Generic Chatbot Guide REST API Reference Zendesk Guide The API key must stay in PHP or a server-side proxy. A key placed in theme JavaScript is publicly readable. Does not cover multisite networks, page caching interactions, or plugin conflict resolution.

pages.body: // Node.js server worker, after webhook authentication and deduplication. async function guardedReply(message) { const hold = { reply: "This reply needs support review.", blocked: true }; try { const baseUrl = process.env.SOTER_BASE_URL; const apiKey = process.env.SOTER_API_KEY; if (!baseUrl || !apiKey) return hold; async function checkedText(path, body, original) { const res = await fetch(baseUrl + path, { method: "POST", headers: { "x-api-key": apiKey, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10000), }); if (!res.ok) throw new Error("Guard unavailable"); const result = await res.json(); if (result?.allowed !== true || !["ALLOW", "ALLOW_WITH_REDACTION", "REWRITE"].includes(result.action)) { throw new Error("Hold for review"); // Includes BLOCK and HUMAN_REVIEW. } const text = result.safeText ?? result.redactedText ?? (result.action === "ALLOW" ? original : null); if (typeof text !== "string" || !text.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing guarded text"); } return text; } const input = await checkedText("/api/guard/input", { message }, message); const draft = await generateReply(input); // Your model adapter; no streaming. const reply = await checkedText("/api/guard/output", { aiResponse: draft }, draft); return { reply, blocked: false }; } catch { return hold; // No original text, guard payload or model draft in this result. } } // Supply userMessage and recipientId from your verified, normalized job. const result = await guardedReply(userMessage); if (result.blocked) return result; // Route to your support/retry queue. await sendWhatsAppReply(recipientId, result.reply); // Your delivery adapter. return result; Integration flow This is a server-side integration pattern for a WhatsApp bot you operate, not a native WhatsApp app or a shipped webhook receiver. You supply the verified webhook handler, model adapter, queue and WhatsApp delivery code. It cannot intercept an unrelated bot's replies. message flow WhatsApp Message → Soter Input Guard → LLM/RAG → Soter Output Guard → WhatsApp Reply 1. Route inbound WhatsApp messages through input guard before the LLM 2. Route model responses through output guard before replying to users 3. Review project PII policy and verify redaction decisions for your supported message formats 4. Add optional security alerts separately; alert delivery is not the gate that blocks a reply Verify the webhook before guarding For direct Meta webhooks, verify X-Hub-Signature-256 using HMAC-SHA256 over the unchanged raw body with your Meta app secret. The GET verification token and challenge handshake is separate; it does not authenticate POST events. [4] Reject invalid signatures before parsing or queueing content, then validate the expected business account and event type. Use a constant-time signature comparison and deduplicate inbound message IDs before generating or sending a reply. If a provider relays WhatsApp for you, implement that provider's authentication contract instead of assuming Meta's headers survive the relay. Keep recipient routing data in your delivery adapter. Phone fields can be absent in newer WhatsApp events; follow Meta's current business-scoped user ID guidance. [5] If you add SoterAI trace identifiers, use an opaque application ID rather than a phone number. The example handles normalized text only, not media, status notifications or every event in a batch. Environment Set both values in the server-side worker. This raw-fetch example has no SDK default. Keep API keys and provider credentials out of browser bundles, logs and source control. server environment SOTER_BASE_URL=https://api.soterai.in SOTER_API_KEY=replace_with_your_server_side_key # Use an HTTPS origin without a trailing slash; never a public client variable. API example Put this inside an async Node.js 18+ worker. generateReply and sendWhatsAppReply are your adapters, not SoterAI APIs. BLOCK, HUMAN_REVIEW, non-success HTTP responses, missing replacement text and network failures withhold delivery. Only an explicit allowed decision continues. A held job still needs your support or retry workflow; it is not the HTTP acknowledgement to Meta. whatsapp-worker.js Before enabling delivery, exercise allowed text, redaction, review, denial, timeout and duplicate events in your own test environment. Buffer the complete model response; do not stream unchecked tokens to WhatsApp. India-specific PII detection The shipped India PII detector uses patterns and context, not identity verification. Project policy determines the action; forward replacement text only after checking the decision. These formats can produce false positives or misses and do not establish regulatory compliance: Aadhaar-like numbers 12 digits with optional spaces or hyphens; not validated as an issued Aadhaar number PAN-like identifiers Five letters, four digits and a final letter UPI IDs Local-part@handle patterns; not an account lookup Indian mobile numbers 10 digits starting 6–9, with optional +91 prefix Bank account-like numbers 9–18 digits with an account or bank-account context label IFSC codes A separate bank-code pattern, not proof of a bank account GSTIN-like identifiers GSTIN-format pattern matching; no registration check What's next? headings.title: Authenticate and normalize events
headings.text: Authenticate and normalize events Intercom signs notifications in X-Hub-Signature with a sha1= prefix: verify HMAC-SHA1 over the unchanged raw body using your Intercom app's client secret, not the SoterAI API key. [2] Reject missing or invalid signatures with a constant-time comparison before parsing or queueing. Validate the expected app, topic and conversation-to-project mapping; deduplicate notification IDs and ignore your own reply events to avoid loops. Queue accepted work and acknowledge delivery separately from AI processing. The sample below does not implement those provider-specific steps. Normalize only the intended customer text; attachments and tool actions need separate checks.

headings.title: Environment
headings.text: Environment Set both values in your server-side worker. These raw HTTP calls do not use an SDK default. Keep Intercom and SoterAI credentials in server secret storage, never in the Messenger browser bundle. server environment SOTER_BASE_URL=https://api.soterai.in SOTER_API_KEY=replace_with_your_server_side_key # Use an HTTPS origin without a trailing slash; do not commit credentials.

headings.title: API usage (server-side)
headings.text: API usage (server-side) Use this inside an async Node.js 18+ worker. You implement generateReply and the Intercom delivery adapter. BLOCK, HUMAN_REVIEW, unknown decisions, HTTP failures, timeouts and missing replacement text hold publication. A held result needs your support or retry queue, not an unchecked fallback draft. intercom-worker.js Test allowed text, redaction, review, denial, API failure and duplicate events before enabling automated replies. Buffer the complete draft; publishing tokens before the output decision bypasses this pattern.

headings.title: Best practices
headings.text: Best practices Use separate projects per client Choose each brand's project API key on your server from authenticated account mappings. A project label alone is not tenant authorization. Always guard output too Run the output guard on AI drafts before they reach customers. Minimize audit logs Prefer allowlisted decision metadata such as action and risk types. Public guard responses can still contain text or matched findings; do not log the whole result. Use webhooks Optional SoterAI alert delivery is separate from Intercom event authentication and must not be your synchronous blocking gate.

(result.action === "ALLOW" ? original : null); if (typeof text !== "string" || !text.trim()) { throw new Error("Missing guarded text"); } return text; } const input = await checkedText("/api/guard/input", { message }, message); const draft = await generateReply(input); // Your model adapter; no streaming. const reply = await checkedText("/api/guard/output", { aiResponse: draft }, draft); return { reply, blocked: false }; } catch { return hold; // Never return the original message or the unchecked draft. } } // Your queue supplies userMessage from an authenticated workflow request. // Only publish result.reply when result.blocked === false; otherwise hand off. return await guardedReply(userMessage); How it works This is a server-side integration pattern, not a native Botpress integration package. The example runs in your authenticated Node.js backend; it is not a universal action or hook you can paste into every Botpress runtime. Your workflow must delegate generation to that backend, or place equivalent checks before its model and send steps. Webchat must never receive the SoterAI key. 1. Input step — Call POST /api/guard/input before the user message reaches your AI agent 2. Output step — Call POST /api/guard/output before the AI response goes to the user 3. Handle decisions — Explicitly branch to a hold/review path for BLOCK, HUMAN_REVIEW, errors and unknown results; do not run later generation or send steps 4. Audit logs — Keep allowlisted decision metadata, not the full guard result; text and matched findings may still be sensitive Environment Set both values server-side. The example uses Node.js 18+ fetch and process.env, not a guaranteed Botpress secret-variable API. If you adapt it to a hosted action, verify that runtime's secret storage, HTTP support and execution limits first. Authenticate workflow requests to your backend; a public, unprotected adapter would expose your quota even if the key stays private. backend environment SOTER_BASE_URL=https://api.soterai.in SOTER_API_KEY=replace_with_your_server_side_key # Use an HTTPS origin without a trailing slash; never a Webchat variable. Botpress workflow example Put this inside an async backend handler. generateReply is your own model adapter. The caller must branch on blocked ; returning an object does not automatically stop a Botpress flow. On an allowed result, send only the returned reply. On a hold, use your review queue or a fixed support message, never the original draft. botpress-backend.js Verify the workflow boundary Exercise allowed text, redaction, review, denial, non-success HTTP responses and timeouts in your own test workflow. Confirm there is no alternate transition that calls the model or sends an unchecked reply after a hold. Buffer the complete draft before output guarding. Attachments, tools, other channels and provider webhook signatures need their own integration-specific checks. Shows the HTTP steps. It does not cover Botpress flow design, NLU training, or channel configuration. Store only the guard verdict in Botpress logs, never the raw text — Botpress logs are not a secure store.

pages.title: Security best practices
pages.summary: Key handling, fail-closed defaults, webhook verification, and OWASP LLM alignment.
pages.body: import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto"; // Read x-soter-signature and the raw request body before JSON parsing. // This verifies dashboard event webhooks, not SIEM webhook exports. function verify(rawBody: string, header: string, secret: string) { const match = /^t=(\d+),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$/.exec(header); if (!match || !secret) return false; const [, timestampText, signature] = match; const timestamp = Number(timestampText); const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000); // Receiver policy: allow at most five minutes of clock skew. if (!Number.isSafeInteger(timestamp) || Math.abs(now - timestamp) > 300) { return false; } const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret) .update(`${timestampText}.${rawBody}`) .digest(); const received = Buffer.from(signature, "hex"); return received.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(received, expected); } // On false: reject the request. On true: parse and validate its JSON, // then deduplicate the verified body.id in durable storage before work. Keep the API key server-side only Use your backend as the integration boundary: browser or mobile client → your authenticated server → SoterAI. The SDK does not replace your application's identity, authorization or abuse controls. Inject SOTER_API_KEY through a server secret store or protected environment. Do not ship it in client JavaScript, mobile binaries or public artifacts. In Next.js, do not use a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix. Read the key only in server code. The WordPress plugin stores its key in server-side options and sends it from PHP. Protect database access, backups and administrator permissions; the frontend uses the local REST proxy. Rotate keys regularly Rotate on your organization's schedule and immediately after suspected exposure. Replace the deployed secret, verify the new key, then revoke the old one. Use distinct ck_test_… and ck_live_… keys for separate environments. The prefix labels a key; it does not create an isolated model, dataset or deployment. Use separate project keys to limit a leak's scope. A supplied project ID or metadata field does not override the project selected by the authenticated key. Always run the output guard Run guardOutput after generation and before release. The output path checks for supported risks such as secret/PII exposure, system-prompt leakage and unsafe content; a clean input verdict says nothing about a later model reply. Require an allowed continuation action. BLOCK , HUMAN_REVIEW , missing decisions and operational failures must not fall through to the original completion. Use returned replacement text for redaction/rewrite decisions. If required replacement text is absent, withhold rather than restoring the original. Return a fixed application refusal on denial or failure. Do not return an unsafe completion alongside blocked: true , and do not expose full guard diagnostics. Buffer output until inspection completes. A check after streaming cannot retract tokens already delivered. For RAG, verify access and grounding separately. The RAG guide distinguishes pre-generation chunk inspection from post-generation checks and session-protected grounding. Redact logs Prefer decision/action, risk category, request ID, latency and failure class over prompt or completion text. The JavaScript client's built-in debug logger emits method/path diagnostics; that does not make application logs, exception messages or entire SDK results safe to persist. Do not log raw prompts, completions, tool arguments, API keys or approval tokens. safeText , redactedText and Python safe_text are not blanket privacy guarantees. Unflagged text may remain unchanged and detections can miss sensitive data. The server's log preparation removes original text for selected confidential risk categories, but can retain non-flagged originals. Review retention, access controls and downstream telemetry independently. When debugging requires content, use synthetic fixtures first. Review and minimize any retained redacted samples under an explicit retention policy. Sign and verify webhooks Dashboard event webhooks send x-soter-signature as t=timestamp,v1=hex_digest . The digest is HMAC-SHA256 over the exact timestamp.rawBody . Read the raw body before JSON parsing; reserializing JSON can change the signed bytes. webhook verification · dashboard events The five-minute timestamp window is receiver policy, not proof against every replay. After verification, validate the payload and deduplicate the signed body's id in durable storage before side effects. Keep receiver clocks synchronized. The separate SIEM webhook exporter uses a different header arrangement. Do not apply this dashboard-event parser to it without checking that integration's contract. Never trust an unsigned header as a substitute for the verified payload. Timeout and fail behavior Configure an end-to-end application deadline that covers guard calls, retrieval, the model and retries. JavaScript timeoutMs defaults to 8,000 milliseconds; Python timeout defaults to 8 seconds. Neither is a whole-conversation latency guarantee. Choose failure policy explicitly. Fail open proceeds without a completed check and favors availability; fail closed withholds work and favors containment. For sensitive output and state-changing tools, prefer fail closed. The core SDKs throw on HTTP/transport failures rather than silently declaring an allow. Catch those errors at your application boundary and return a fixed public response, not the exception message or original text. JavaScript retries / maxRetries defaults to zero and covers network failures and 5xx responses. Python max_retries also defaults to zero but retries transport exceptions, not HTTP 5xx/429 responses. Bound retries and distinguish guard retries from model/tool retries. A timed-out write may already have happened; use application idempotency and reconciliation rather than blindly repeating it. Rate limiting and abuse prevention Respect 429 and Retry-After . SDK rate-limit exceptions expose the delay as JavaScript retryAfter or Python retry_after ; retries are not an authorization bypass. Add per-user/IP limits at your public endpoint and cap body size, message length, retrieval fan-out and tool invocations. SoterAI's API-key rate limit does not distinguish your own end users. The server uses Redis-backed counters when configured, with a process-local fallback when Redis is absent or unavailable. Limits in fallback mode are per instance, not a distributed quota. Monitor that degraded state in multi-instance deployments. Known limitations Detection has false positives and false negatives. Test representative benign and adversarial inputs for your language, model, policy and data. Use OWASP LLM risks as a review checklist. An implemented check or passing local regression is not a SOC 2/ISO 27001 certificate or independent security assessment. Combine these checks with least privilege, input validation, output encoding, secrets management, monitoring and incident response. Validate tool restrictions and retrieval authorization separately. This reduces risk; it does not guarantee complete protection. Do not turn an integration example into a claim of universal production readiness. Release verification Exercise allow, redaction, block, human review, malformed requests, throttling and outages. Assert the downstream action count and the exact public response, not just a detector label. Keep results tied to the SDK/server versions and policy actually deployed. What's next? Quickstart Guide API Contract ← CLI Quickstart → Practices, not a compliance certificate. Following them does not make a deployment SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certified. Complements secure design, identity controls, monitoring, and incident response. It does not replace any of them.
